The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 75f6af00a38589bf), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: For every fixed λ > 0 there are constants η > 0, B < ∞, and a fixed finite list of bounded-arity test laws with the following properties. From a Boolean 3CNF formula one can construct, in polynomial time, a finite uniform space S of bit positions and these test laws on S. (i) Every individual question marginal is at most B times uniform measure on S. All samplers are polynomially enumerable finite weighted lists with rational probabilities; every positive seed probability is at least inverse-polynomial in the input size. (ii) If the formula is satisfiable, there is an assignment y : S → F2 accepted by every test in every support. (iii) If the formula is unsatisfiable, every assignment fails one of the test laws with probability greater than η. (iv) There is also an exchangeable law of (s1, s2, s3, s4) ∈ S4 , with uniform marginals, such that the conditional expectation operator of any coordinate given any other has norm at most λ on mean-zero L2 (S). The assignment in (ii) satisfies ys1 + ys2 + ys3 + ys4 = 0 in F2 throughout the support of this law. All constants, including the degrees of the polynomial size and time bounds, depend only on λ. Two independent copies of the law in (iv), paired coordinatewise, have the same pair-operator bound on S2 and give the corresponding parity identity for the expressions yi + yj.
